editorial:
You follow a time-traveling agent on his final mission to catch a bomber who keeps slipping through the years. The story pulls you in with a strange bar conversation that slowly reveals a wild, layered life story. You meet a man with a painful past whose journey connects to the agent in ways you will not see coming. The vibe is dark, twisty, and full of surprises that keep you guessing until the very end.

Ethan Hawke is solid, but Sarah Snook steals the show with a powerful, layered performance that carries the whole film. The pacing is tight and never wastes a scene. Pros include a clever plot, strong acting, and great twists. Cons: it can get confusing if you stop paying attention, and the time loops grow complicated. Best for fans of smart sci-fi. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn the agent, the Fizzle Bomber, and John are all the same person at different points in time. The agent travels back and becomes the bomber he was hunting, creating a closed loop. Jane gives birth to herself, and the agent recruits his younger self. Everything loops endlessly with no true beginning. The twist means the mission was always doomed to repeat.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart time-travel stories and big twists.
